title: Neural ECG classifier reduces inconclusive readings across four devices
summary: A prospective diagnostic study compared a residual neural classifier with four device algorithms against physician-interpreted ECGs. Among 824 recordings from 206 patients, inconclusive results fell from 16% to 1.2%. This selected hospital study does not establish population-screening or workload benefit.

evidence.tested: Near-contemporaneous physician-interpreted 12-lead references; blinded adjudication. Training contained no smart-device recordings.
evidence.unknown: 52 of 258 recruited patients lacked complete recordings. Selected electrophysiology patients, vectorized exports and unrepeated inconclusive recordings limit generalization. Four recordings per participant are correlated. Vendor-affiliated authors participated; no clinical-outcome benefit tested.
evidence.ai_role: A trained residual CNN classifies rhythm from raw single-lead signals.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary clinical/model Methods, Results and limitations; exact front/date/current PubMed notices.
